vocabulary.example: I work out at the gym every day.
I want to lose weight this year.
My goal is to run a marathon.
How long have you been exercising?

grammar.explanation_en: Present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) emphasizes an activity that started in the past and continues now, focusing on duration: 'I have been exercising for two months.' It's often used with 'How long' questions.
grammar.explanation_ko: 현재완료 진행형(have/has been + 동사-ing)은 과거에 시작해 지금까지 계속되는 활동을 강조하며, 지속 기간에 초점을 둡니다: 'I have been exercising for two months.'(2개월째 운동해오고 있어요). 'How long' 질문과 자주 함께 쓰입니다.

examples.en: I have been going to the gym for three months.
She has been training for the marathon since spring.
examples.ko: 그녀는 봄부터 마라톤 훈련을 해오고 있어요.

examples.en: How long have you been doing yoga?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: You look great! How long have you been working out?
dialogue.line_ko: 보기 좋아 보여요! 운동한 지 얼마나 됐어요?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: I've been going to the gym for four months now.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: I want to gain muscle and run a 10K race.

reading.title: My Fitness Journey
reading.text: I have been exercising for six months now. At first, my legs were sore every day, but I have gotten used to it. My goal is to lose weight and gain muscle. I have been working with a personal trainer since March, and I already feel much stronger.
reading.text_ko: 저는 6개월째 운동을 해오고 있어요. 처음에는 매일 다리가 근육통이었지만, 이제는 익숙해졌어요. 제 목표는 살을 빼고 근육을 키우는 거예요. 3월부터 개인 트레이너와 함께 하고 있고, 벌써 훨씬 강해진 느낌이에요.

explanation.en: The text says 'I have been exercising for six months now.'
The text says 'my legs were sore every day.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'my legs were sore every day'라고 나옵니다.
